papers.title: The Construction and Practice of AI-Supported Contextualized Teaching in Chinese Language Education
papers.abstract: The incorporation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into education marks a major shift and presents new methods for making improvements on learning. This paper looks into the building and practical application of an AI-powered contextualized education model, targeted specially for Chinese language teaching. Contextual teaching that stresses on learning within actual situations is regarded as a great way to teach for decades, but still it encounters problems regarding the limited resources, lack of dynamic interactivity, and personalization at large scale. This research claims that AI, such as NLP, intelligent tutoring system, machine learning adaptation and VR, will be able to solve the problem. we come up with a framework that uses AI really well to create immersive, individualized, and engaging learning situations where active learning can be encouraged. An empirical study lasting one academic semester was carried out with 120 middle school students, which were distributed into two groups: experimental and control, where the experimental group was taught by using the AI-assisted model of teaching, and the group taught with traditional methods served as the control. The data collected was from pre/post-tests, engagement surveys, in-class observations, semi-structured teacher interviews. The results showed that compared with the control group, the experimental group achieved great improvement on all aspects, especially communicative competence and cultural understanding. From the analysis of the test scores, it can be seen that there is an obvious increase in scores for the experimental group (p < 0.01). More so, students in the AI-supported environment reported higher motivations, confidences and engagements. It brings useful information and a workable guideline to teachers trying to bring AI into language courses, changing how we teach Chinese so it’s not just about moving information around but creating a fun, filled-with-context lesson that helps with all parts of language and learning to like the culture deeply.

papers.title: ANALYSIS OF PROJECT BASED LEARNING (PjBL) METHODS TO IMPROVE VOCATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS' LEARNING ACTIVENESS
papers.abstract: Abstract: This study aims to determine: (1) the process of Project Based Learning Methods to increase the active learning of Vocational High School students. (2) The application of learning methods can increase the learning activity of vocational high school students. This type of research is descriptive research, which is a research that seeks to answer existing problems based on data from national articles as well as international articles and source books. This research data is secondary data consisting of books, theses, national articles, and international articles. The data collection technique in this research is by using a documentation study. The data obtained in this study were analyzed using the data analysis of the Miles and Huberman model consisting of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. The results of this study based on previous research studies or research that has been done show that there are two types of research carried out in the process of applying the Project Based Learning method, namely classroom action research and quasi-experimental. 4 articles using classroom action research and 1 article using a quasi-experimental research design with pretest-posttest control group design. The classroom action research of these four articles was carried out in three cycles. In the first cycle the researcher will apply the Project Based Learning learning method during the learning process, after the first cycle ends, an evaluation and assessment of student activity will be carried out. This evaluation will be used as improvement material for cycles II and III. The next step is to do cycles II and III with the same steps as cycle I. A quasi-experimental research from one article was carried out with a pretest-posttest control group design. In the first stage the researcher will conduct a pretest to determine the initial ability of students from the aspect of student activity. The next stage is the researcher applies the Project Based Learning method during the learning process in the classroom. After that, the researcher will carry out a posttest to determine the final ability of students from the aspect of student activity. The results of the study based on previous research studies indicate that the use of Project Based Learning learning methods can increase the activeness of students in the classroom. papers.title: Leveraging AI for Sustainable and Cost-Effective Decentralized Energy in Rural U.S. Regions
papers.abstract: Sustainable and affordable decentralized power in rural parts of the U.S. is difficult to accomplish because of inadequate infrastructure and transmission costs, and centralized grids are susceptible. This paper suggests an artificial intelligence (AI) hybrid framework combining XGBoost and a neural network to provide precise predictions of renewable generation and operational expenses. More than 13000 electric power plants databases in the United States underwent preprocessing in order to solve the problem of missing data, heterogeneity, and rural-urban disparities. The proposed model (XGBoost+NN) was compared with KNN, Auto encoder, PINN, CNN-LSTM, and BiLSTM-Attention. It out-performed all baselines with MSE of 0.0003, RMSE of 0.0178, R2 of 0.999, and MAPE of 1.36%. The error in predicting costs was only 0.08% and this is both a technical strength and an economic importance. These findings indicate the model’s scalability, interpretability, and possible use to facilitate equitable access to clean and affordable energy in underserved rural populations.
